column9:
These are not negative points, just some observations on the test cases to help constructively:

In Test Case 1 - the expected result "Expected results: The note is saved successfully and appears in the list of notes." If any span appears indicating that the note was saved, it would be good to include this in the expected result. This way, it implies that when clicking save note, no user notification will appear and the note will appear in the list of notes. Also, inform if the user would be redirected after saving the card (as was done in the cancelation TC).

In TC 3, there is a test for adding an audio file, I believe the TC for recording audio is missing.

I feel the need to have the same basic card creation tests for the other types (reversed card and optional reversed card), and this could be specified in the TC description or steps, whichever is preferred

column8:
The suite addresses a range of important functionalities, from basic operations, such as adding text and images, to more advanced functionalities, such as using tags and media support.
There is a good inclusion of edge cases, such as Test Case 5, which checks the maximum character limit, and Test Case 9, which tests unsupported image formats. Test Case 4, which verifies the behavior when leaving fields empty, and Test Case 9, which tests adding images in unsupported formats, ensure that the application handles user errors well, improving both the experience and reliability. In addition to verifying that the application functions correctly, the tests also cover usability aspects, such as in Test Case 7, which checks data retention and UI adaptation after device rotation
column9: Absence of security tests, such as protection against malicious data input (e.g., script injection). Also, there are no tests aimed at evaluating the application's performance when handling large amounts of data, such as creating many notes or displaying multiple items in the notes list.

Test cases 1, 2, and 3 cover something in the expected result that is already tested in test case 4, which may be confusing to identify the issue, since if test case 4 fails, the previous ones will always fail as well.

Test cases 7 and 8 leave open what invalid values are for the fields. If someone reads the suite, they may only test with letters and forget to test with negative numbers.
